'''Daniele Cherniak''' is an American geochemist known for her work on using [[particle beam]]s for geochemical analysis on small scales. She was elected a fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]] in 2021.

== Education and career ==
Cherniak grew up in [[Cohoes, New York]] and went to Keveny Memorial Academy.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Kurp|first=Patrick|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mYhGAAAAIBAJ&dq=%22Daniele+Cherniak%22&pg=PA36&article_id=6720,6524428|title=RPI physicist goes ultra when it comes to running|publisher=The Daily Gazette|date=April 28, 1996|language=en}}</ref> In 1983, Cherniak received her  undergraduate degree from [[Union College]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=January 1, 1999|title=Just keep running and running|url=https://muse.union.edu/newsarchives/1999/01/01/just-keep-running-and-running/|access-date=October 3, 2021|website=Union College News Archives|language=en-US}}</ref> and went on to earn her Ph.D. in physics at the [[University at Albany, SUNY]] in 1990.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=A particle accelerator based study of major and trace element diffusion in minerals|url=https://www.worldcat.org/title/particle-accelerator-based-study-of-major-and-trace-element-diffusion-in-minerals/oclc/%7B%7B%7B24077047%7D%7D%7D|date=1990|language=English|first=Daniele J|last=Cherniak}}</ref> As of 2021, she is a research professor at [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=collaborators|url=https://homepages.rpi.edu/~watsoe/collaborators.htm|access-date=October 4, 2021|website=homepages.rpi.edu}}</ref> and works at the [[Ion beam|Ion Beam]] Lab at the [[University of Albany|University at Albany]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ion Beam Lab – People|url=https://www.albany.edu/ionbeamlab/people/IBL_assoctiates.shtml|access-date=October 4, 2021|website=www.albany.edu}}</ref>

== Research ==
Cherniak is known for her research on rock-forming minerals, specifically on [[atomic diffusion]] in these minerals.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Daniele Cherniak Honored With 2021 Walt Westman Award {{!}} News & Events|url=https://news.rpi.edu/approach/2021/03/26|access-date=October 3, 2021|website=news.rpi.edu}}</ref> She established the use of [[ion implantation]] to place lead into minerals followed by the use of [[Rutherford backscattering spectrometry]] to obtain diffusion profiles, which she first applied to measurements in [[apatite]] and [[zircon]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cherniak|first1=D.J|last2=Lanford|first2=W.A|last3=Ryerson|first3=F.J|date=1991|title=Lead diffusion in apatite and zircon using ion implantation and Rutherford Backscattering techniques|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/001670379190137T|journal=Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta|language=en|volume=55|issue=6|pages=1663–1673|doi=10.1016/0016-7037(91)90137-T|bibcode=1991GeCoA..55.1663C|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and has subsequently applied to other minerals.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cherniak|first1=D.J|last2=Ryerson|first2=F.J|date=1993|title=A study of strontium diffusion in apatite using Rutherford backscattering spectroscopy and ion implantation|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0016703793901908|journal=Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta|language=en|volume=57|issue=19|pages=4653–4662|doi=10.1016/0016-7037(93)90190-8|bibcode=1993GeCoA..57.4653C|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cherniak|first=D.J.|date=1993|title=Lead diffusion in titanite and preliminary results on the effects of radiation damage on Pb transport|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/000925419390253F|journal=Chemical Geology|language=en|volume=110|issue=1–3|pages=177–194|doi=10.1016/0009-2541(93)90253-F|bibcode=1993ChGeo.110..177C|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She has also examined the diffusion of [[rare-earth element]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cherniak|first1=D.J.|last2=Hanchar|first2=J.M.|last3=Watson|first3=E.B.|date=1997|title=Rare-earth diffusion in zircon|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0009254196000988|journal=Chemical Geology|language=en|volume=134|issue=4|pages=289–301|doi=10.1016/S0009-2541(96)00098-8|bibcode=1997ChGeo.134..289C|url-access=subscription}}</ref> tetravalent cations,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cherniak|first1=D. J.|last2=Hanchar|first2=J. M.|last3=Watson|first3=E. B.|date=May 28, 1997|title=Diffusion of tetravalent cations in zircon|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s004100050287|journal=Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology|volume=127|issue=4|pages=383–390|doi=10.1007/s004100050287|bibcode=1997CoMP..127..383C|s2cid=96293255|issn=0010-7999|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and oxygen<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Watson|first1=E|last2=Cherniak|first2=D|date=1997|title=Oxygen diffusion in zircon|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0012821X97000575|journal=Earth and Planetary Science Letters|language=en|volume=148|issue=3–4|pages=527–544|doi=10.1016/S0012-821X(97)00057-5|bibcode=1997E&PSL.148..527W|url-access=subscription}}</ref> into zircon. Her work on argon<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Watson|first1=E. Bruce|last2=Thomas|first2=Jay B.|last3=Cherniak|first3=Daniele J.|date=2007|title=40Ar retention in the terrestrial planets|url=http://www.nature.com/articles/nature06144|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=449|issue=7160|pages=299–304|doi=10.1038/nature06144|pmid=17882213|bibcode=2007Natur.449..299W|issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription}}</ref> showed that the degassing of Earth is slower than expected.<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 24, 2007|title=Argon Provides Atmospheric Clues|url=https://www.terradaily.com/reports/Argon_Provides_Atmospheric_Clues_999.html|access-date=October 4, 2021|website=www.terradaily.com}}</ref> Much of her work is collaborative projects with [[E. Bruce Watson]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Watson|first=E. Bruce|date=April 1, 2019|title=Acceptance of the 2018 Roebling Medal of the Mineralogical Society of America|url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.2138/am-2019-AP10443/html|journal=American Mineralogist|language=en|volume=104|issue=4|pages=621–622|doi=10.2138/am-2019-AP10443|bibcode=2019AmMin.104..621W|s2cid=132248194|issn=0003-004X|url-access=subscription|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2020, she began a project working with scientists Union College on a study of [[radioactive decay]] which will improve both disposal of nuclear waste and increase precision of dating material that is billions of years old.<ref>{{Cite web|date=March 1, 2020|title=Union professor leads research that could help improve nuclear waste disposal {{!}} The Daily Gazette|url=https://dailygazette.com/2020/03/01/union-professor-leads-research-that-could-help-improve-nuclear-waste-disposal/|access-date=October 3, 2021|website=dailygazette.com}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Cherniak started running cross country while in high school<ref name=":0" /> and continued to run while at Union College.<ref name=":1" /> Cherniak runs in [[ultramarathon]]s<ref name=":0" /> and has earned team bronze medals in 1998<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rpNGAAAAIBAJ&dq=%22Daniele+Cherniak%22&pg=PA17&article_id=5667,1264675|title=The Sunday Gazette|publisher=The Sunday Gazette|date=November 5, 1998|language=en}}</ref> and 2000<ref>{{Cite web|title=2000 IAU World Challenge 100 km|url=http://www.americanultra.org/100k2000/|access-date=October 4, 2021|website=www.americanultra.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C3ghAAAAIBAJ&dq=%22Daniele+Cherniak%22&pg=PA15&article_id=3725,124782|title=The Daily Gazette|publisher=The Daily Gazette|date=September 1, 2001|language=en}}</ref> in the [[IAU 100 km World Championships]]. Her local running club, Hudson Mohawk Road Runners Club,<ref>{{Cite web|date=March 2020|title=Meet Our Runners :: Hudson-Mohawk Road Runners Club|url=https://www.hmrrc.com/members/pacesetter/2020/march/meet-our-runners|access-date=October 3, 2021|website=www.hmrrc.com|language=en}}</ref> elected her to their hall of fame for her running accomplishments,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Current Hall of Fame members|url=https://www.hmrrc.com/application/files/6216/3163/1787/Current_Hall_of_Fame_members091121.pdf}}</ref> the first woman to receive this honor.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Daniele Cherniak: New Editorial Assistant for The Pace Setter :: Hudson-Mohawk Road Runners Club|url=https://www.hmrrc.com/members/pacesetter/2019/november/daniele-cherniak-new-editorial-assistant-pace-setter|access-date=October 3, 2021|website=www.hmrrc.com|language=en}}</ref>

Cherniak also volunteers for the Spindle City Historic Society<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 2014|title=Spindle City Newsletter|url=https://www.spindlecity.net/NewsLetters/2010-4-Winter.pdf|access-date=October 3, 2021}}</ref> in Cohoes, New York and has been recognized for her work in historic preservation in the area, especially in the restoration of parts of the [[Erie Canal]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 18, 2012|title=Cohoes to participate in state's Heritage Weekend|url=https://www.saratogian.com/news/cohoes-to-participate-in-states-heritage-weekend/article_431cc096-d59b-525a-b5e9-b6144bd8f24b.html|access-date=October 4, 2021|website=Saratogian|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=June 20, 2011|title=Cohoes digs for a glorious past|url=https://www.timesunion.com/local/article/Cohoes-digs-for-a-glorious-past-1431199.php|access-date=October 3, 2021|website=Times Union|language=en-US}}</ref>
